about: Which <send target> values name a Mesh peer, written out by hand.
A target is a Mesh peer when it is `#` followed by at least one character
and that character is not `_`: `#_` stays reserved for the targets
The same answer is computed in four places - the C++ core's
(which decides at code-generation time which sends to lower to the Mesh
router), and the Rust and Kotlin routers' mesh_peer / meshPeer (which
refuse a request that is not one). A target one of them routes over Mesh
and another does not would be the same document meaning two things, so
